title: The Lake of Skeletons
facts: Roopkund is a high‑altitude glacial lake in the Himalayas at 5,020 m (16,470 ft) elevation in Chamoli District, Uttarakhand, India.
The lake is seldom more than 40 m in diameter, covering about 1,000‑1,500 m², and is about three metres deep.
Skeletons were rediscovered in 1942 by forest ranger Hari Kishan Madhwal of Nanda Devi National Park.
Radiocarbon dating shows one group of remains dates to around 800 CE (±30 years) and another to around 1800 CE.

Genomic analysis identified three ancestry groups: ~23 individuals with South‑Asian ancestry (~800 CE), one individual with Southeast‑Asian ancestry (~1800 CE), and 14 individuals with eastern‑Mediterranean ancestry (~1800 CE).
Local legend attributes the deaths to a sudden hailstorm that killed a pilgrimage party led by Raja Jasdhaval and Rani Balampa in the 9th century.
When the ice melts for about one month each year, the skeletal remains become visible in the clear water of the shallow lake.
Tourists have been removing bones, prompting district officials to call for protection of the site.

lines.say: In 1942, a ranger discovers a frozen lake.
Radiocarbon dates one group to 800 CE.
Genomic analysis shows South‑Asian, Southeast‑Asian, and eastern‑Mediterranean ancestries.
Legend speaks of a hailstorm killing pilgrims.
Its discoverer believed the storm caused the deaths.
The lake sits at 5,020 m, a high‑altitude basin.
Tourists remove bones, prompting officials to protect the site.
Skeletons are older than pyramids, yet no metal, no wheel, no writing.
